answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, switching primary vendor (memory_c2 showed quick onboarding, but that was unconstrained and unverified for current conditions) or deferring past expiry in 14 days both add delivery risk. Negotiating terms with the incumbent directly targets the 18% mandate — memory_c4 shows benchmarking moved the incumbent on price and payment terms, and memory_c6 shows multi-year volume commitments cut unit cost without narrowing service scope — while memory_c1 shows renewal keeps integration stable with no interruption. Adding a second source (memory_c3) is valuable insurance but doesn't meet the cost-cut mandate this cycle and consumes the single decision slot. I want to verify memory_c2 (how deep the low-cost vendor savings actually were, to use as a credible benchmark/threat in negotiation) and memory_c4 (the mechanics of the successful renegotiation). Confidence is moderate pending archive confirmation; if verification shows the low-cost vendor gap was very large, a hybrid (negotiate with credible switch threat) remains within the negotiate_terms action.
